title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #5

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Claves are (1 mark)
   A. a horn
   B. two wooden sticks hit together
   C. a kind of flute
   D. drums with strings

2. What is the first step in improvising an accompaniment to a song? (1 mark)
   A. Change the words
   B. Stop singing
   C. Find the steady beat
   D. Buy a drum

3. Isukuti is a lively drum dance of the (1 mark)
   A. Somali
   B. Turkana
   C. Luhya
   D. Maasai

4. What is the correct order for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Burn, cut, trim, cool
   B. Cut, trim, burn, cool
   C. Cool, burn, trim, cut
   D. Trim, cool, burn, cut

5. What is the correct way to catch a netball? (1 mark)
   A. With your eyes closed
   B. With one hand held stiff
   C. With your feet
   D. With two hands, giving with the ball

6. How many players are in a full netball team on the court? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 7
   C. 11
   D. 5

7. When is an overhead pass most useful? (1 mark)
   A. When shooting from far
   B. When a defender is standing close
   C. When resting
   D. When you are alone on the court

8. Which of these is a dark tone of red? (1 mark)
   A. Red mixed with a little black
   B. Red mixed with yellow
   C. Red mixed with white
   D. Red mixed with water

9. In a montage, the subject matter means (1 mark)
   A. the price of the paper
   B. the colour of the desk
   C. what the montage is about
   D. the size of the glue pot

10. How many beats does each bar have in the four-beat patterns of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Four
   C. Two
   D. Six

11. What does a crotchet look like? (1 mark)
   A. A filled-in oval with a stem
   B. A dot only
   C. A zigzag
   D. An empty circle

12. Listening for the name of a note without seeing it is called (1 mark)
   A. painting
   B. running
   C. aural work
   D. drawing

13. A melody is (1 mark)
   A. the loudness
   B. the beat of a drum
   C. the words only
   D. the tune of a song

14. Which is a good ratio of length to height for a flag drawing? (1 mark)
   A. One to one
   B. Three to two
   C. Two to three tall
   D. Ten to one

15. What is patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Fear of runners
   B. Love of food
   C. A kind of race
   D. Love for one's country

16. What happens on the command set? (1 mark)
   A. The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   B. The runners run
   C. The race ends
   D. The runners sit

17. The top stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. black
   B. white
   C. red
   D. green

18. Compared with the medium start, the elongated start has the back knee (1 mark)
   A. further back
   B. in the air
   C. on the line
   D. further forward

19. In a crab balance, your tummy faces (1 mark)
   A. down
   B. up
   C. sideways
   D. backwards

20. Why is gymnastics described as not being a race? (1 mark)
   A. It uses no body
   B. It cannot be seen
   C. It is about control and quality, not speed
   D. It is always in the dark

21. What is the last part of the sequence in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Rolling backwards
   B. Getting up slowly and standing tall
   C. Jumping
   D. Running away

22. What should you do if something hurts during gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Push a friend
   C. Keep going
   D. Stop and tell your teacher

23. A folk song is (1 mark)
   A. a song without a message
   B. a computer song
   C. a traditional song belonging to a community
   D. a song only for cities

24. Unison singing is suitable for an anthem because (1 mark)
   A. everyone can join in the same tune
   B. it needs instruments
   C. it uses no notes
   D. it is silent

25. What should you do about distracting things behind the subject? (1 mark)
   A. Photograph them too
   B. Remove them or change the angle
   C. Ignore them always
   D. Add more

26. When you blow into the recorder, the sound is made by (1 mark)
   A. air vibrating inside it
   B. the wood being struck
   C. a drum skin
   D. a string

27. What sound do you hear if a hole is not fully covered? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing at all
   B. A drum sound
   C. A squeak or weak sound
   D. A clear note

28. Uncovering holes makes the note (1 mark)
   A. silent
   B. lower
   C. the same
   D. higher

29. Which joint has the mouthpiece? (1 mark)
   A. Middle joint
   B. None
   C. Head joint
   D. Foot joint

30. Tonguing means (1 mark)
   A. rolling on the floor
   B. saying too or doo quietly at the start of each note
   C. singing loudly
   D. chewing

31. Why should you not dive into shallow water? (1 mark)
   A. It makes splashes
   B. It makes noise
   C. It looks silly
   D. You can hit the bottom and hurt your head or neck

32. Which is a rule for water games? (1 mark)
   A. Play alone
   B. Do not hold anyone under water
   C. Ignore the whistle
   D. Dunk friends

33. Prone means (1 mark)
   A. standing
   B. face up
   C. sitting
   D. face down

34. The giraffe stretch mainly improves (1 mark)
   A. flexibility
   B. smell
   C. hearing
   D. only speed

35. Why do animal games often use singing or drumming? (1 mark)
   A. To scare animals
   B. To stop the game
   C. Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   D. To hide the players

36. Which of these is a national day on which the anthem is sung? (1 mark)
   A. Sports day only
   B. Birthday of a friend
   C. Market day
   D. Jamhuri Day

37. When someone comments on your work, you should (1 mark)
   A. argue
   B. tear the work
   C. listen quietly and say thank you
   D. walk away

38. Verse 3 of the anthem talks about (1 mark)
   A. cooking
   B. the weather
   C. working together to build the nation and giving thanks
   D. sports

39. What is used to close a homemade portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. Nails
   B. A string or ribbon tie
   C. A padlock
   D. Wet glue only

40. Every displayed work should have (1 mark)
   A. a secret code
   B. a price only
   C. no name
   D. a label with the title and artist's name

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe the position of the back knee in the medium start and in the elongated start. (3 marks)

42. State how many finger holes a descant recorder has in front and where the thumb hole is. (2 marks)

43. Explain where the sun should be when you photograph a person and why. (3 marks)

44. Write the rhythm names of a pattern of a crotchet, a crotchet rest, a pair of quavers and a crotchet. (3 marks)

45. Why is it important to appreciate the works of people from different cultures? (3 marks)

46. Give four steps of a double-handed catch. (4 marks)

47. How should you give feedback on a friend's photograph? (3 marks)

48. What does singing in unison mean? Why is it good for an anthem? (3 marks)

49. What does it mean to appreciate a work of Creative Arts? (2 marks)

50. State what red, white and the shield stand for on the Kenyan flag. (3 marks)

51. State three values taught by the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

52. State three qualities of a good melody. (3 marks)

53. Name four guide lines used for free hand lettering. (4 marks)

54. Why should you delete poor photographs from a device? (3 marks)

55. Compose a four-beat rhythmic pattern using a crotchet, a pair of quavers and a rest, and write it in rhythm names. (4 marks)

56. What is the difference between a working portfolio and a display portfolio? (2 marks)

57. Why should a short melody end on d? (2 marks)

58. List four steps of the medium start. (4 marks)

59. Write a melody that goes up by steps from d to m and comes down to d, and state the number of notes. (3 marks)

60. Name the three secondary colours and state how each is made. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #5 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — two wooden sticks hit together
   Claves are two hardwood sticks that are struck together.

2. C — Find the steady beat
   You must find the beat before you can add patterns.

3. C — Luhya
   Isukuti is played by the Luhya people, especially the Isukha and Idakho.

4. B — Cut, trim, burn, cool
   The stages are cutting, trimming, burning, then cooling.

5. D — With two hands, giving with the ball
   A double-handed catch with elbows bending as the ball arrives is correct.

6. B — 7
   A full netball team has seven players on court.

7. B — When a defender is standing close
   The ball goes over the defender's arms.

8. A — Red mixed with a little black
   Adding black makes a darker shade of red.

9. C — what the montage is about
   The subject matter is the theme.

10. B — Four
   The patterns of this lesson have four beats.

11. A — A filled-in oval with a stem
   A crotchet has a filled note head and a stem.

12. C — aural work
   Aural work uses the ears to identify notes.

13. D — the tune of a song
   A melody is a series of notes that make a tune.

14. B — Three to two
   A flag rectangle is about one and a half times as long as it is high.

15. D — Love for one's country
   Patriotism is love and respect for one's country.

16. A — The runners raise their hips slightly and stay still
   On set, runners lift the hips and hold still.

17. A — black
   Black is at the top, red in the middle and green at the bottom.

18. A — further back
   Elongated means longer, so the feet are further apart.

19. B — up
   The tummy faces the ceiling like a table top.

20. C — It is about control and quality, not speed
   Skill and control matter more than speed.

21. B — Getting up slowly and standing tall
   Finish by standing up slowly with control.

22. D — Stop and tell your teacher
   Pain is a warning, so stop and tell the teacher.

23. C — a traditional song belonging to a community
   Folk songs are passed on by singing.

24. A — everyone can join in the same tune
   A single tune that everybody sings is simple and strong.

25. B — Remove them or change the angle
   A plain background keeps attention on the subject.

26. A — air vibrating inside it
   The air inside vibrates.

27. C — A squeak or weak sound
   Leaks make squeaks.

28. D — higher
   Shorter air column means a higher note.

29. C — Head joint
   The mouthpiece is at the top of the head joint.

30. B — saying too or doo quietly at the start of each note
   Tonguing separates notes clearly.

31. D — You can hit the bottom and hurt your head or neck
   Shallow water is dangerous for diving.

32. B — Do not hold anyone under water
   Safety first.

33. D — face down
   Prone is face down.

34. A — flexibility
   Stretching increases flexibility.

35. C — Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   Music sets the pace.

36. D — Jamhuri Day
   Jamhuri Day is a national holiday.

37. C — listen quietly and say thank you
   Good listeners grow.

38. C — working together to build the nation and giving thanks
   It calls for common effort and gratitude.

39. B — A string or ribbon tie
   Punched holes with string keep it closed.

40. D — a label with the title and artist's name
   Labels help viewers.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: In the medium start, the back knee is level with the middle of the front foot. In the elongated start it is level with the heel of the front foot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each position, 1 mark for saying the elongated start is further back.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Seven finger holes in front and the thumb hole is at the back.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Behind the photographer, so light falls on the front of the person. If the sun is behind the subject, the face is in shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 2 marks for the reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: taa (rest) ta-te taa
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part in order.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: We learn about others, it builds respect and unity and it helps us value all cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Watch the ball into your hands; reach out with both hands; spread the fingers with the thumbs close; bend the arms and pull the ball to the chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say what you like first, comment on light and centre of interest, and suggest one improvement politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone sings the same notes at the same time. It is simple and everybody can join in together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning, 2 marks for the reason.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: To notice, understand and value it, giving reasons for what you think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Red stands for the blood shed for freedom. White stands for peace and honesty. The shield and spears stand for the defence of freedom.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Unity, peace, justice, hard work, service, patriotism and thankfulness to God. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stepwise motion, variation of syllables and note lengths, and ending on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ascender line, top of small letters, baseline and descender line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: To save memory space, keep only good pictures and make it easier to find the best ones.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example taa ta-te (rest) taa. Any four-beat pattern with all three parts and ending on a crotchet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four beats, 1 mark for using all three, 1 mark for correct names, 1 mark for ending on a long note.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: A working portfolio holds work in progress. A display portfolio holds the best finished works for showing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: d is the home note. Ending on it makes the melody sound finished.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each idea.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Front foot about one and a half foot lengths behind the line; kneel on the rear knee level with the middle of the front foot; hands behind the line shoulder-width apart; on set, lift the hips a little above the shoulders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: d r m r d. There are five notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for going up, 1 mark for coming down, 1 mark for five.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Orange from red and yellow, green from yellow and blue, purple from blue and red.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each secondary colour with its mixture.
